subject: HyperCloud vs Redwood: post-demo gap analysis & bench plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HyperCloud vs Redwood: post-demo gap analysis & bench plan

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap from my side and a suggested next step so we can close the performance questions for your infra team:

What we heard
- Acme wants to validate latency under expected traffic (burst to 250 rps) and tail latency at p95/p99 for interactive assistants (avg seq len ~96 tokens).
- You’re currently evaluating HyperCloud’s managed inference API in parallel with a self-managed setup. Key comparison points are latency consistency, tokens/sec at 8xA100 equiv, and behavior under KV-cache warmup.

What Redwood can do next (proposal)
1) We run a head-to-head A/B bench using the same model family and identical prompt set (you provide the canonical prompt set; we can use the 1000 sample file attached as a starting bucket).
2) Test matrix: 3 payload sizes (32, 96, 256 tokens), concurrency sweep (1, 8, 32), and a sustained run for 30 minutes to capture p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
3) Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail-throughput (tokens/sec aggregated), cold vs warmed KV cache, and cost-per-token estimate.

Deliverables & timeline- Draft test plan and data capture spec (attached PDF).- Run in our dedicated test harness + run the same harness against HyperCloud endpoints you share.- Deliver a short results deck with reproducible scripts and raw output.

Ask: Can you confirm the contact who can share the HyperCloud endpoint details and any egress restrictions? Also please drop the canonical prompt set or give us permission to use the attached sampling.

I’ll coordinate with Vivek and Rafael on the bench config once we have the endpoint. If it’s helpful, Rafael can propose smaller quickchecks first (30 minute smoke) before the full run.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

Neha —

Appreciate the clear write-up. Priya is looped for the HyperCloud endpoint details; Priya, can you share the staging API key + an endpoint we can use for non-prod benchmarking (we’ll redact keys after the run)?

A few notes from our infra side:
- Typical interactive traffic peaks at ~180 rps but we want headroom to 250 rps.
- Sequence distribution: ~60% short (<=32), 30% medium (~96), 10% long (>=256).
- We care a lot about p99 stability — some user flows are very sensitive to spikes.

I’m fine with the plan — smoke run first, then the 30-minute sustained. We should also capture end-to-end request time from the app layer (so we can compare network+api vs pure inference).

I’ll send the prompt set and a staging JSON bundle by EOD.

—Tom
Director of Product, Acme Health
Tom.Reynolds@acmehealth.com

Quick internal -> external summary and proposed immediate steps:

@Neha / Tom — thanks for the prompt details. Rafael and I sketched a pragmatic test harness:
- Runner: k6 with a lightweight wrapper that records server-side timestamps and per-token counts.
- Models: use a single open-family model across both providers (we recommend the L-latest-8k equivalent for parity).
- Metrics emitted: per-request latency, token_count, cpu/gpu util, and external request-retcode. We’ll surface p50/p95/p99 and a rolling 1-minute p99 to show spikes.

Smoke plan (next 48 hours):
1) Small smoke: 15 minutes at 8 concurrent sessions, sequences sampled per your distribution.
2) If smoke looks sane, full run: 30 minutes at steady 180 rps target with 60s ramp to 250 rps peak.

Action items:
- Tom: confirm you’ve uploaded the prompt bundle to the Drive link & confirm whether we should also hit your in-app telemetry endpoint for E2E timing.
- Priya: confirm the staging endpoint will accept our k6 agent IPs (we’ll provide ranges).
- Rafael: I’ll assign the bench job once network ACLs are confirmed.

I’ll capture configs and post run results into the shared Drive folder.

—Vivek
Head of Performance, Redwood Inference
